# STcompare

STcompare compares the spatial gene expression patterns of two spatial
transcriptomics (ST) datasets of structurally matched tissues, location
by location. It finds genes whose spatial pattern differs between, for
example, a diseased and a healthy tissue, including differences that a
comparison of mean expression misses. The documentation website is
[jef.works/STcompare](https://jef.works/STcompare/).

## Overview

![Overview of STcompare: simulated kidneys A, B and C compared by
differential gene expression, by spatial correlation with empirical
p-values, and by spatial
similarity](https://github.com/JEFworks-Lab/STcompare/blob/main/images/overview_figure1.png?raw=true)

Differential gene expression analysis compares mean expression and
ignores where a gene is expressed. In the simulated example above, the
spatially distinct patterns A and B have the same mean expression, so
they are not differentially expressed, while the spatially similar
patterns A and C differ in their mean, so they are. STcompare
distinguishes these cases with two tests, for every gene:

| Test                    | Question                                                     | Output                                                                                                             |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Spatial correlation** | Is the spatial pattern of the gene the same in both samples? | Pearson’s correlation over matched locations, with a permutation p-value that accounts for spatial autocorrelation |
| **Spatial similarity**  | Is the expression level the same at matched locations?       | The share of matched locations whose values are within a fold change of each other                                 |

The usual test of Pearson’s correlation assumes that observations are
independent, but neighbouring locations in a tissue have similar
expression, so its p-values are far too small for spatial data.
STcompare computes the null distribution from surrogates of each sample
that keep its spatial autocorrelation (Viladomat et al. 2014) and the
gene’s own distribution of values, with permutations that stop early for
genes that are clearly not significant.

STcompare compares the same locations in the two samples, so the samples
must be:

1.  **aligned**, so that the same coordinates point to the same
    structure in both tissues, for example with
    [STalign](https://github.com/JEFworks-Lab/STalign);
2.  **rasterized together** onto one grid of pixels with
    [SEraster](https://github.com/JEFworks-Lab/SEraster), so that a
    pixel refers to the same location in both samples.

## Installation

STcompare needs R 4.5 or later. Install it from GitHub with BiocManager,
which also installs the Bioconductor packages that STcompare depends on
(it uses the remotes package for GitHub):

``` r
install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
BiocManager::install("JEFworks-Lab/STcompare")
```

STcompare contains C++ code, so the installation needs a C++17 compiler:
the Xcode command line tools on macOS (`xcode-select --install`),
[Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) on Windows, or
the C++ compiler of your Linux distribution. See
[Installation](https://jef.works/STcompare/articles/Install.html) for
details.

## Quick start

This example runs in a few seconds:

``` r
library(STcompare)

# three simulated kidneys: A and B have opposite patterns,
# A and C the same pattern at different levels
data(speKidney)

# rasterize the samples together, onto one grid of hexagonal pixels
rast <- SEraster::rasterizeGeneExpression(speKidney, assay_name = "counts",
                                          resolution = 0.2, fun = "mean",
                                          square = FALSE)

# compare A and B: both tests, for every gene
res <- compareSpatial(rast[c("A", "B")], nThreads = 2)
res

# the standard figure of a gene: the cells, the pixels, the similarity
# classes and the matched pixels with the statistics
plotGene(res, "Gene", rast$A, rast$B, native = speKidney[c("A", "B")])
```

The result has one row per gene, with the correlation `correlationCoef`,
its permutation p-value `pValuePermute`, that p-value adjusted across
genes `pValuePermuteAdj` (the one to call a gene significant), the
similarity `percentSimilarity`, and diagnostics. The columns have the
names of the legacy functions;
[`?compareSpatial`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/compareSpatial.md)
and [Getting
started](https://jef.works/STcompare/articles/getting-started-with-STcompare.html)
explain every one of them.

[`plotGene()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/plotGene.md) draws
one figure for a gene, ready to save with
[`ggplot2::ggsave()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggsave.html),
and `plotOverview(res)` the overview of all the genes of a result:

![The standard figure of Gene for the simulated kidneys A and B: the
cells of each kidney coloured by expression (A), the shared pixels
coloured by expression (B), the pixels coloured by similarity class (C),
and a scatter plot of the values at matched pixels with the correlation,
the p-values and the similarity (D)](reference/figures/plotGene.png)

## Tutorials and articles

- [Getting started with
  STcompare](https://jef.works/STcompare/articles/getting-started-with-STcompare.html):
  both tests on simulated data, how to read the results, and why the
  permutation p-values are needed.
- Case studies that run the published analyses in a minute or two:
  - [Acute kidney injury (10x
    Visium)](https://jef.works/STcompare/articles/acute-kidney-injury-10x-visium-rasterized.html)
  - [Comparison of MERFISH and Visium for mouse
    brain](https://jef.works/STcompare/articles/brain-MERFISH-10x-visium.html)
- [How STcompare
  works](https://jef.works/STcompare/articles/how-STcompare-works.html):
  the tests step by step.
- [Parameters, performance and
  reproducibility](https://jef.works/STcompare/articles/parameters-performance-reproducibility.html):
  choosing the settings, run times, threads and seeds.
- [Function reference](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/index.html)

## Citation

`citation("STcompare")` gives the reference, also in BibTeX:

Kalen Clifton, Vivien Jiang, Rafael dos Santos Peixoto, Srujan Singh,
Ryo Matsuura, Hamid Rabb, Jean Fan, STcompare: comparative spatial
transcriptomics data analysis of structurally matched tissues to
characterize differentially spatially patterned genes, *Bioinformatics*,
Volume 42, Issue 9, September 2026, btag644,
<https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btag644>

The spatial correlation test builds on Júlia Viladomat, Rahul Mazumder,
Alex McInturff, Douglas J. McCauley, Trevor Hastie, Assessing the
significance of global and local correlations under spatial
autocorrelation: a nonparametric approach, *Biometrics*, Volume 70,
Issue 2, June 2014, Pages 409-418, <https://doi.org/10.1111/biom.12139>

## Getting help

Please report bugs and ask questions on the [issue
tracker](https://github.com/JEFworks-Lab/STcompare/issues).

# Package index

## Compare two samples

The main function: the spatial correlation test and the spatial
similarity for every gene, and the methods of its result.

- [`compareSpatial()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/compareSpatial.md)
  : Compare the spatial expression patterns of genes between two samples
- [`print(`*`<STcompareResult>`*`)`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/STcompareResult.md)
  [`summary(`*`<STcompareResult>`*`)`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/STcompareResult.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.STcompareResult>`*`)`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/STcompareResult.md)
  [`` `[`( ``*`<STcompareResult>`*`)`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/STcompareResult.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<STcompareResult>`*`)`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/STcompareResult.md)
  : Methods for compareSpatial() results

## Spatial correlation, legacy functions

The correlation functions of earlier versions. They reproduce the
published analyses exactly.

- [`spatialCorrelationGeneExp()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/spatialCorrelationGeneExp.md)
  : Spatial correlation test for every gene of two samples
- [`spatialCorrelationGeneExpIterPermutations()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/spatialCorrelationGeneExpIterPermutations.md)
  : Spatial correlation test with more permutations for promising genes
- [`spatialCorrelationGeneExpWithinSample()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/spatialCorrelationGeneExpWithinSample.md)
  : Spatial correlation test between pairs of genes of one sample
- [`spatialCorrelation()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/spatialCorrelation.md)
  : Spatial correlation test of two vectors of values at the same
  locations
- [`viladomatCorrelation()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/viladomatCorrelation.md)
  : Spatially autocorrelated surrogates and permutation p-value for one
  direction

## Visualization

Standard figures of a compareSpatial() result: one gene with its maps,
similarity classes and statistics, and the overview of all genes. The
legacy functions plot single genes from the results of the legacy
functions.

- [`plotGene()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/plotGene.md) :
  Standard figure of one gene in a compareSpatial() result
- [`plotOverview()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/plotOverview.md)
  : Overview figure of a compareSpatial() result
- [`linearRegression()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/linearRegression.md)
  : Plot a gene's values in two samples, coloured by similarity class
- [`pixelClass()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/pixelClass.md)
  : Map the similarity class of every pixel
- [`plotCorrelationGeneExp()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/plotCorrelationGeneExp.md)
  : Plot a gene's values in two samples at the shared pixels
- [`savePlots()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/savePlots.md) :
  Maps, pixel classes and scatter plot of genes, optionally saved as PDF

## Spatial similarity, legacy function

The similarity with the class of every pixel.

- [`spatialSimilarity()`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/spatialSimilarity.md)
  : Computes spatial similarity of gene expression between two
  SpatialExperiments.

## Example data

- [`speKidney`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/speKidney.md) :
  Simulated Kidney SpatialExperiment Data
- [`simRanPatternRasts`](https://jef.works/STcompare/reference/simRanPatternRasts.md)
  : Simulated Random Spatially Patterned Kidney Datasets
